subject.title: Support Slack user-level events (events on behalf of users) for DM routing

question: Should OpenClaw support an explicit Slack user-identity mode that receives user-authorized `message.im` events and replies through the configured user token as that Slack user?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the permanent behavior changes Slack identity, authorization, auditability, and token-selection semantics, so automation should not choose the boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
options.body: Add a named opt-in mode with authorization routing, reply-token selection, security docs, tests, and live Slack proof while keeping bot identity as the default.

options.title: Keep Slack bot identity only
options.body: Document that Slack user tokens are for read and lookup support, not for natural no-app-badge user impersonation.

options.title: Defer pending live proof
options.body: Ask for a redacted Socket Mode transcript proving user-level DM envelopes reach OpenClaw before deciding whether the mode should exist.

recommendation.title: Support explicit user-identity mode
recommendation.body: Add a named opt-in mode with authorization routing, reply-token selection, security docs, tests, and live Slack proof while keeping bot identity as the default.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest current history signal around Slack identity, Socket Mode filtering, and monitor/provider behavior.
